lessons: The harness must launch the real squatch serve (squatch/serve.py) on a tmp copy of hosts/fixture/. Injecting serve/confirm as caller callables that return literal strings is fabricated evidence and gets rejected.

Send machine-actor confirm requests through the real control-inbox writer (squatch/control.py). Take each observable and producing_run from the journal entries and run records that serve writes in the tmp host. Only the clock, process, filesystem and provider seams may be faked.

Record each of the at least three machine-ticket merges as its own entry with its own scenario, observable and producing_run. The validator should require at least three distinct producing runs for machine_ticket_merges, not exactly one entry per member.

Criterion 3: in test_host_loop, test_stages and test_gates, run the real construction path (FixtureHostLoop.run(), stage runs, ordinary lift). Then assert that no host-loop-report.json or exit-receipt.json exists under the repo, the workspace or tickets/*.

Read squatch/serve.py, squatch/control.py and the hosts/fixture/ scenarios before writing the harness. The last attempt used 18 of 75 budgeted minutes and skipped the engine integration that the ticket requires.
Keep the closed HostLoopEntry, HostLoopReport and ExitReceipt schemas and their KNOWN_ARTIFACTS registration; review found them sound. Change only the entry cardinality.
reason: Review findings name concrete, fixable gaps with paved roads (a stubbed harness, one entry covering all merges, no-artifact tests that check nothing). The attempt used a fraction of its budget, so this was a shortcut, not a capability limit.
